stops.note: 'understanding', from intellegere 'to perceive'; Cicero's De Inventione lists it with memory and foresight as the three parts of prudence
the philosopher Karol Libelt, in his 1844 essay 'On Love of the Fatherland', used it for the educated class that should lead the partitioned nation
the novelist Pyotr Boborykin claimed to have brought the word into Russian in the 1860s; it came to mean the radical, reform-minded educated class
Western writers adopted it for Russia's intellectuals around the 1905 Revolution, then for intellectuals anywhere

current_meaning: intellectuals considered as a group or class
